text.title: Growth Experiment Design Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Growth Experiment Design. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: The dashboard is checked daily; the test is stopped on day four "because it reached significance"; the shipped change shows no lift in the following month.

root-cause.source: Johari et al., 'Peeking at A/B Tests' (KDD 2017)

antipattern.root-cause: No stop date was fixed before launch and a fixed-horizon test was read repeatedly, multiplying the false-positive rate.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-fixed-stop-date-no-peeking-srm-check`: record the stop date from the sample-size calculation; hide the results panel until then or declare a sequential method up front.

antipattern.symptom: Planned 50/50 shows 47/53 on tens of thousands of users; the result is reported anyway and looks strongly positive.

root-cause.source: Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020)

antipattern.root-cause: Assignment or exposure logging was broken (a redirect dropping slow clients, a bot filter on one arm) and nobody checked the ratio before reading the metric.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-fixed-stop-date-no-peeking-srm-check`: the SRM chi-square check is recorded before any metric is read; p below 0.001 invalidates the run and sends it back to instrumentation.

antipattern.symptom: "We launched the new onboarding Monday and activation is up 15 percent versus last week" is filed as an experiment win; the same week a campaign started.

root-cause.source: Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020)

antipattern.root-cause: No randomised control group; the comparison baseline was time, which also carried every other change.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-control-group-randomised-by-flag`: assignment through the flag platform with a concurrent control; pre/post comparisons are labelled observations and excluded from the experiment log.

antipattern.symptom: The spec listed "engagement"; the write-up reports the one of six metrics that moved; next quarter a different metric is the headline.

root-cause.source: Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020)

antipattern.root-cause: No single primary metric was committed before launch, so the analysis selected the winner among many.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rules `r-hypothesis-falsifiable-with-effect-size` and `r-one-primary-metric-plus-guardrails`: one named primary metric with a minimum effect in the hypothesis; every other metric is a guardrail with a stop threshold, not a candidate headline.

antipattern.symptom: A 3 percent lift on a 2 percent conversion rate is tested on 4,000 users for one week; the result is "not significant" and the idea is killed.

root-cause.source: Widely established practice in statistical power analysis

antipattern.root-cause: Sample size was never computed; the duration was set by the sprint calendar.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-sample-size-computed-before-launch`: compute the sample from baseline, MDE, alpha and power; if the duration exceeds eight weeks, redesign for a larger effect or a proxy metric instead of launching.

antipattern.symptom: The variant changes the checkout page; exposure is logged at session start for every visitor; the measured lift is a fraction of what the checkout funnel itself shows.

root-cause.source: Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020), on triggering

antipattern.root-cause: The playback step was skipped, so nobody noticed that 80 percent of "exposed" users never reached the changed screen.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-instrumentation-playback-before-ramp`: fire and verify the exposure event at the moment of seeing the variant, with experiment and variant ids, before ramping past the smoke-test cohort.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a Growth Experiment Design output (launching the experiment, ramping allocation, shipping the winner), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
